implementationReview.summary: Reviewed kitchen.py (the only sourceManifest entry) against all five M12 requirements. The implementation uses only the Python standard library, wires a global --store option before subcommands, performs read-only loads for list/can-cook queries, validates pantry amounts (nonnegative int, zero retained), validates recipe ingredients (nonempty object, nonempty string names, positive ints with booleans rejected), computes can-cook shortfalls without persisting, and only saves after a sufficient-stock cook check. All stated behaviors are statically decidable from the source.

reviewerJudgements.reason: kitchen.py imports only argparse, json, and sys; --store is registered on the top-level parser before subcommands; _load_store opens the file read-only and list/can-cook branches never call _save_store; success paths print one JSON object to stdout with ensure_ascii=False and exit implicitly 0, while _fail routes diagnostics to stderr and exits 1.

pantry list returns the pantry dict (defaulting to an empty object on missing store); pantry set parses an int, rejects negative values, retains zero, stores the amount, and returns name and amount fields.

recipe list returns the recipes dict (defaulting to an empty object initially); recipe add parses INGREDIENTS_JSON as a nonempty object of nonempty string names whose amounts are positive ints (booleans explicitly rejected), persists it, and returns name and ingredients fields.

can-cook looks up the recipe, computes per-ingredient shortfalls against pantry amounts, returns can_cook and missing fields without saving; cook computes the same missing set, fails before mutating pantry when insufficient, and only subtracts quantities and persists after the sufficiency check, returning a cooked field.

Unknown recipe, insufficient stock, malformed ingredient JSON, and nonpositive/boolean ingredient amounts all route through _fail (stderr and exit 1) before any _save_store call; cook only persists after the sufficiency check, so a failed cook leaves bytes unchanged and consumes nothing. Persistence is via per-invocation JSON files keyed by the supplied --store path, isolating stores across processes.

pantry list returns the pantry dict (defaulting to an empty object on missing store); pantry set parses an int, rejects negative values, retains zero, stores the amount, and returns name and amount fields.

recipe list returns the recipes dict (defaulting to an empty object initially); recipe add parses INGREDIENTS_JSON as a nonempty object of nonempty string names whose amounts are positive ints (booleans explicitly rejected), persists it, and returns name and ingredients fields.

can-cook looks up the recipe, computes per-ingredient shortfalls against pantry amounts, returns can_cook and missing fields without saving; cook computes the same missing set, fails before mutating pantry when insufficient, and only subtracts quantities and persists after the sufficiency check, returning a cooked field.

Unknown recipe, insufficient stock, malformed ingredient JSON, and nonpositive/boolean ingredient amounts all route through _fail (stderr and exit 1) before any _save_store call; cook only persists after the sufficiency check, so a failed cook leaves bytes unchanged and consumes nothing. Persistence is via per-invocation JSON files keyed by the supplied --store path, isolating stores across processes.
